definitions.explanation: The number 700. {七|なな} + {百|ひゃく}, with no sound change.

examples.japanese: {七百|ななひゃく}{円|えん}の{本|ほん}を{買|か}った。
この{村|むら}の{人口|じんこう}は{七百|ななひゃく}{人|にん}ほどだ。
examples.english: This village has a population of about 700.

examples.japanese: {山頂|さんちょう}まではあと{七百|ななひゃく}メートルだが、ここからが{一番|いちばん}{急|きゅう}だ。
examples.english: It is another 700 meters to the summit, but the steepest part starts here.

notes:
{七|なな} + {百|ひゃく}. Both parts keep their normal shape.

READING NOTE:
The alternative しちひゃく is possible but rarely used; なな is preferred throughout the hundreds because しち is easily misheard as いち. The same preference shows up in {七時|しちじ} versus {七人|しちにん}／{七人|ななにん}, where speakers often choose なな for clarity.

SOUND CHANGES IN THE HUNDREDS:
Only {三百|さんびゃく}, {六百|ろっぴゃく}, and {八百|はっぴゃく} change; {七百|ななひゃく} and the rest are regular.
